from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'Imagine a drone scouting a remote target area.',
            'The drone reports coordinates using its internal tilted map.',
            'It sees the target at position three, two.',
            'But ground control uses a standard square grid.',
            'We need to translate between these different perspectives.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Misunderstood Scout Drone", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        GOLD = "#FFD700"
        CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        GRAY = "#666666"

        # Center of the grid area for reference
        tl = self.grid['A1']
        br = self.grid['F6']
        center_point = (tl + br) / 2

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        
        # Standard Grid
        standard_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1], y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            x_length=5, y_length=5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GRAY, "stroke_width": 1},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": WHITE, "stroke_width": 1.5}
        )
        self.place_in_area(standard_grid, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        # Target Point at visual (0, 3) relative to the center_point
        # We manually place it on the grid system to ensure alignment
        target_dot = Dot(color=GOLD, radius=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(target_dot, 'B4') # Positioned in the upper region
        
        self.play(Create(standard_grid))
        self.play(FadeIn(target_dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(CYAN)
        )
        
        # Tilted Grid
        drone_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1], y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            x_length=5, y_length=5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": CYAN, "stroke_width": 1, "stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": CYAN, "stroke_width": 2}
        ).rotate(PI/6)
        self.place_in_area(drone_grid, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(drone_grid))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CYAN)
        )
        
        # Label Drone: (1,2)
        drone_label = Text("Drone: (1,2)", color=CYAN, font_size=20)
        # Position label near target
        self.place_at_grid(drone_label, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        drone_label.next_to(target_dot, LEFT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Write(drone_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GOLD)
        )
        
        # Label Standard: (0,3)
        standard_label = Text("Standard: (0,3)", color=GOLD, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(standard_label, 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        standard_label.next_to(target_dot, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        # Visual emphasis on standard grid
        self.play(
            Write(standard_label),
            standard_grid.animate.set_stroke(width=3, color=WHITE),
            drone_grid.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Restore clarity to both
        self.play(
            standard_grid.animate.set_stroke(width=1.5, color=WHITE),
            drone_grid.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        )
        
        # Highlight Basis vectors at origin
        origin_ref = center_point
        std_i = Arrow(origin_ref, origin_ref + RIGHT * 0.5, buff=0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        std_j = Arrow(origin_ref, origin_ref + UP * 0.5, buff=0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        
        drone_i = Arrow(origin_ref, origin_ref + (RIGHT*np.cos(PI/6) + UP*np.sin(PI/6)) * 0.5, buff=0, color=CYAN, stroke_width=4)
        drone_j = Arrow(origin_ref, origin_ref + (LEFT*np.sin(PI/6) + UP*np.cos(PI/6)) * 0.5, buff=0, color=CYAN, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(Create(std_i), Create(std_j))
        self.play(Create(drone_i), Create(drone_j))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Configuration
        TITLE = "Prerequisite Review: The Standard Basis"
        LINES = [
            'Our standard grid uses perpendicular vectors i and j.',
            'Coordinates are scalars multiplying these two basis vectors.',
            'Vector three, two means three right, two up.'
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(TITLE, LINES)
        
        # Dim all lines initially
        for line in self.lecture:
            line.set_color(GRAY_D)

        # Colors
        COLOR_I = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_J = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_V = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_GRID = "#666666"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight current line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Define Coordinate System
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": COLOR_GRID, "stroke_opacity": 0.6},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": WHITE, "include_tip": True}
        )
        
        # Basis Vectors - Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency
        i_vec = Vector([1, 0], color=COLOR_I)
        j_vec = Vector([0, 1], color=COLOR_J)
        i_label = Text("i", font_size=24, slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_I).next_to(i_vec, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        j_label = Text("j", font_size=24, slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_J).next_to(j_vec, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Group everything for proper placement in the right area
        world = VGroup(plane, i_vec, j_vec, i_label, j_label)
        self.place_in_area(world, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Animation: Fade in grid and basis vectors
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_vec), Write(i_label), run_time=1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(j_vec), Write(j_label), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Change lecture color
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY_D)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Equation: v = 3i + 2j
        # Constructing as VGroup of Text to mimic MathTex indexing for the later scalar animation
        equation = VGroup(
            Text("v", slant=ITALIC), 
            Text("="), 
            Text("3"), 
            Text("i", slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_I), 
            Text("+"), 
            Text("2"), 
            Text("j", slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_J)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        equation.set_color(WHITE)
        equation[3].set_color(COLOR_I)
        equation[6].set_color(COLOR_J)
        
        # Place equation in the upper part of the animation area
        self.place_at_grid(equation, 'A4', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Change lecture color
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY_D)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Draw the components on the grid
        origin = plane.get_origin()
        unit_x = plane.get_x_unit_size()
        unit_y = plane.get_y_unit_size()
        
        # 3 units along i
        step_i = Line(origin, origin + RIGHT * 3 * unit_x, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=4)
        # 2 units along j starting from the end of step_i
        step_j = Line(origin + RIGHT * 3 * unit_x, origin + RIGHT * 3 * unit_x + UP * 2 * unit_y, color=COLOR_J, stroke_width=4)
        
        # The resultant vector V
        v_vec = Arrow(origin, plane.coords_to_point(3, 2), buff=0, color=COLOR_V)
        v_label = Text("v = (3, 2)", font_size=24, slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_V).next_to(v_vec.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        # Animate the path
        self.play(Create(step_i), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(step_j), run_time=1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_vec), Write(v_label))
        
        # Final highlight on scalars in equation (matching previous indexing)
        scalar_3 = equation[2]
        scalar_2 = equation[5]
        
        self.play(
            scalar_3.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(YELLOW),
            scalar_2.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(YELLOW),
        )
        self.play(
            scalar_3.animate.scale(1/1.2),
            scalar_2.animate.scale(1/1.2),
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the scene layout
        title = "Defining a New Perspective (The New Basis)"
        lines = [
            "Any two independent vectors can form a new basis.",
            "A Forest Ranger might use these skewed basis vectors.",
            "This creates a tilted coordinate system for their map."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Color mapping for lines
        COLOR_B1 = "#FF8C00"
        COLOR_B2 = "#1E90FF"
        COLOR_GRID = "#8B4513"
        
        # Visual Origin and Vectors
        origin_pos = self.grid["D3"]
        b1_vec_raw = np.array([2, 1, 0])
        b2_vec_raw = np.array([-1, 1, 0])
        
        # Standard basis for transition
        i_vec = Arrow(origin_pos, origin_pos + RIGHT, buff=0, color=WHITE)
        j_vec = Arrow(origin_pos, origin_pos + UP, buff=0, color=WHITE)
        
        # New basis vectors
        b1_vec = Arrow(origin_pos, origin_pos + b1_vec_raw, buff=0, color=COLOR_B1)
        b2_vec = Arrow(origin_pos, origin_pos + b2_vec_raw, buff=0, color=COLOR_B2)
        
        # Labels - Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid 'latex' dependency
        label_b1 = Text("b1", color=COLOR_B1)
        label_b2 = Text("b2", color=COLOR_B2)
        label_basis = Text("Basis B", color=COLOR_GRID)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_B1))
        
        # Show standard basis first
        self.play(Create(i_vec), Create(j_vec))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Replace i and j with b1 and b2
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(i_vec, b1_vec),
            ReplacementTransform(j_vec, b2_vec),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight second line, dim first
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_B2)
        )
        
        # Label the new vectors
        self.place_at_grid(label_b1, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b2, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(label_b1), Write(label_b2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight third line, dim second
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_GRID)
        )
        
        # Create skewed grid
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        # Lines parallel to b1
        for k in range(-2, 3):
            # We want the lines to cover the right side area roughly
            line_b1 = Line(
                origin_pos + k * b2_vec_raw - 1.2 * b1_vec_raw,
                origin_pos + k * b2_vec_raw + 1.5 * b1_vec_raw,
                color=COLOR_GRID,
                stroke_opacity=0.4,
                stroke_width=2
            )
            grid_lines.add(line_b1)
        
        # Lines parallel to b2
        for k in range(-1, 3):
            line_b2 = Line(
                origin_pos + k * b1_vec_raw - 2.0 * b2_vec_raw,
                origin_pos + k * b1_vec_raw + 2.0 * b2_vec_raw,
                color=COLOR_GRID,
                stroke_opacity=0.4,
                stroke_width=2
            )
            grid_lines.add(line_b2)
            
        # Ensure grid is behind vectors
        self.add_foreground_mobjects(b1_vec, b2_vec, label_b1, label_b2)
        
        # Label Basis B
        self.place_at_grid(label_basis, "F5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Create(grid_lines), Write(label_basis), run_time=2.5)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Clean up highlights for final state
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial layout setup
        lines = [
            'Change of basis is just a coordinate transformation.',
            'It makes complex problems easier by changing the lens.',
            'One vector, two names, one shared world.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Intuition Wrap-up", lines)
        
        # Define matrix P (Basis B transformation)
        matrix_p = [[1.2, 0.4, 0], [0.3, 0.9, 0], [0, 0, 1]]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#58C4DD"), run_time=0.5)

        # Replace MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        # Since the system environment lacks a LaTeX distribution, we use Text for the formula.
        formula = Text(
            "[v]_std = P [v]_B", 
            color="#FFFFFF",
            font_size=28
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A1', 'A6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Setup the standard grid
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": "#666666",
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.6
            },
            axis_config={"stroke_color": "#888888"}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B1', 'E6', scale_factor=0.9)
        plane.save_state() # Save standard grid state
        
        # Reference vectors (stationary in world space)
        # We shift them to the plane's center so they align with its coordinate origin
        vec_red = Vector([1, 1], color="#FC6255").shift(plane.get_center())
        vec_blue = Vector([-1, 0.5], color="#58C4DD").shift(plane.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            Write(formula),
            Create(plane),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            GrowFromPoint(vec_red, plane.get_center()),
            GrowFromPoint(vec_blue, plane.get_center()),
            run_time=1.0
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight second lecture line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#83C167"),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        # Smoothly morph the standard grid into the slanted Basis B grid
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_p, about_point=plane.get_center()),
            run_time=2.5,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight third lecture line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        # Morph the grid back to standard
        self.play(
            Restore(plane),
            run_time=2.0,
            rate_func=smooth
        )

        # Display the final takeaway: 'Basis is just a choice of language'
        takeaway = Text(
            "Basis is just a choice of language", 
            color="#FFFF00", 
            font_size=28
        )
        self.place_in_area(takeaway, 'F1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(takeaway))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Change of Basis: Viewing the Same World Through Different Lenses

sections.title: The Hook: The Misunderstood Scout Drone
sections.content: Introduce the motivation for change of basis. Use a visual scenario where two observers describe the same object's position differently because they are using different reference grids.
sections.example: A scout drone sees a 'Target' at coordinates (3, 2) on its tilted, non-standard internal map. However, the ground control station needs the coordinates on their standard square grid map. How do we translate the drone's language to ours?

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Standard Basis
sections.content: Briefly revisit the standard basis vectors i(1, 0) and j(0, 1). Visualize the standard Cartesian grid with perpendicular lines and unit length 1. Emphasize that coordinates are just scalars multiplying these vectors.
sections.example: Visualizing vector V = 3i + 2j as taking 3 steps along the x-axis and 2 steps along the y-axis.

sections.title: Defining a New Perspective (The New Basis)
sections.content: Introduce a 'New Basis' (B) consisting of two vectors, b1 and b2, that are not the standard i and j. Explain that any set of linearly independent vectors can form a 'language' to describe space.
sections.example: Show a 'Forest Ranger' character who uses basis vectors b1 = (2, 1) and b2 = (-1, 1). On screen, draw these as skewed, colored arrows forming a slanted grid.

sections.title: The Core Concept: One Vector, Two Names
sections.content: Explain that a vector is a physical arrow in space that doesn't change, but its 'name' (coordinates) changes depending on which grid lines we follow to reach its tip.
sections.example: Animate a point in space. Show how to reach it by following 1 unit of b1 and 2 units of b2. To the Ranger, the vector is [1, 2]_B. To us, we calculate its 'Standard' position by summing those vectors.

sections.title: The Transition Matrix (The Translator)
sections.content: Introduce the Transition Matrix 'P'. This matrix contains the new basis vectors (b1, b2) as its columns. Explain that multiplying a vector's 'New Basis' coordinates by P converts them into 'Standard Basis' coordinates.
sections.example: Form matrix P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]]. Multiply P by the Ranger's coordinates [1, 2]. Result: [0, 3]. Visual: The slanted grid coordinate (1, 2) aligns perfectly with standard coordinate (0, 3).

sections.title: Reverse Engineering: Changing to the New Basis
sections.content: Show the reverse process. If we have standard coordinates and want the Ranger's coordinates, we use the Inverse Matrix (P⁻¹).
sections.example: A deer is at standard position (4, 5). We multiply [4, 5] by P⁻¹ to tell the Ranger exactly where to look on their custom tilted map.

sections.title: Summary and Intuition Wrap-up
sections.content: Recap the main formula: [v]_standard = P * [v]_basis_B. Reinforce the idea that Change of Basis is just a 're-scaling' and 'skewing' of the coordinate system to make certain problems easier to solve (like in computer graphics or physics).
sections.example: Animate the standard grid morphing into the slanted grid and back, showing the vector arrow remaining stationary while the background grid changes.

storyboard.title: The Hook: The Misunderstood Scout Drone
lecture_lines: Imagine a target located at these standard coordinates.
A drone views this using a tilted internal map.
One point now has two different sets of coordinates.
animations: A target point appears at standard coordinates (0, 3) in gold (#FFD700).
A tilted grid (#00FFFF) fades in; the same point now has different relative coordinates.
Text labels 'Standard: (0,3)' and 'Drone: (1,2)' appear to highlight the conflict.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: The Standard Basis
lecture_lines: Our standard grid uses basis vectors i and j.
We reach vector V using three i and two j.
Coordinates are just scalars scaling these basis vectors.
animations: Standard grid (#666666) appears with basis vectors i (#FF0000) and j (#00FF00).
Vector V (3, 2, #FFFFFF) is drawn as a combination of 3i and 2j.
The coordinates (3, 2) are highlighted as scalars multiplying the basis vectors.

storyboard.title: Defining a New Perspective (The New Basis)
lecture_lines: We can choose any two independent vectors as basis.
These new vectors define a slanted coordinate grid.
We call this new coordinate system Basis B.
animations: Replace i and j with new vectors b1 (2, 1, #FF8C00) and b2 (-1, 1, #1E90FF).
A skewed grid (#8B4513) is drawn using b1 and b2 as the new unit directions.
The new coordinate system is labeled as 'Basis B'.

storyboard.title: The Core Concept: One Vector, Two Names
lecture_lines: A physical vector is a fixed arrow in space.
In our standard grid, we call it zero, three.
But the slanted grid offers a different perspective.
We reach the same tip using one b1, two b2.
This same vector is named one, two in Basis B.
animations: A stationary white vector arrow (#FFFFFF) is shown against a dark background, with the ground [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ground.svg] positioned at the bottom.
Standard grid (#666666) appears, showing the vector's name is [0, 3] here.
The standard grid fades out and the slanted Basis B grid fades in.
Animate steps along b1 and b2 (1*b1 + 2*b2) to reach the vector tip.
Label the vector as [1, 2] in Basis B, emphasizing it's the same arrow.

storyboard.title: The Transition Matrix (The Translator)
lecture_lines: Matrix P stores the new basis vectors as columns.
We represent the new coordinates as a column vector.
Multiplying by P translates between these two languages.
The calculation returns our familiar standard coordinates.
Both coordinate systems describe the exact same point.
animations: Vectors b1 and b2 move to form the columns of matrix P (#FFFF00).
The coordinates [1, 2] from Basis B are written as a column vector.
The matrix P multiplies the column vector [1, 2] with step-by-step arithmetic.
The result [0, 3] appears, matching the standard basis coordinates.
Visual transition: The slanted grid coordinate (1, 2) aligns with standard (0, 3).

storyboard.title: Reverse Engineering: Changing to the New Basis
lecture_lines: To find new coordinates from standard ones...
...we multiply by the inverse of matrix P.
The grid morphs, revealing the vector's new name.
animations: A new point 'Deer' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/deer.svg] appears at standard position (4, 5) in light green (#98FB98).
Display the inverse matrix P^-1 (#FFA07A) used to 'go back' to Basis B.
The standard grid morphs to Basis B, showing the deer [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/deer.svg] at coordinates (3, 2)_B.

storyboard.title: Summary and Intuition Wrap-up
lecture_lines: This formula links any two coordinate systems together.
Basis vectors define how we measure the world.
Changing basis is like looking through a different lens.
The world stays fixed; only our description changes.
Ultimately, basis is just a choice of language.
animations: Display the formula [v]_std = P * [v]_B in bold white (#FFFFFF).
Show the standard grid (#666666) with multiple reference vectors [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/world.svg].
Smoothly morph the standard grid into the slanted Basis B grid.
Morph the grid back to standard, keeping the vectors fixed in space.
Display the final takeaway: 'Basis is just a choice of language' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lens.svg].
